You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order. Each sentence carries, in square brackets, the heading it was written under. File every sentence under that heading. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

S3 [SUBJECTIVE]: When the patient aroused this morning, he was warm to the touch.

S5 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: Additionally, I suggested trying Zarbee’s for children under 1 years old.
S6 [SUBJECTIVE]: Cough, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea.

S11 [SUBJECTIVE]: Treatment has included saline nasal spray, Tylenol, baby Vick's, and a humidifier.
S12 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: If a croup cough develops, the patient will receive a 0.5 teaspoon.
S13 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: Additionally, he may also use baby oil and a soft brush on the area.
S14 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: The patient presents with a viral infection and does not need antibiotics currently.

S16 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: I recommended Head and Shoulders shampoo, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral A-D 2 times per week, combined with his usual shampoo.
S17 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: Return in one week for a re-check.
S18 [SUBJECTIVE]: The patient has been exposed to an older sister who is sick and a cousin who has a sinus infection.
S19 [SUBJECTIVE]: When his sleeper was removed, he was quite sweaty despite the air conditioner being on.
S20 [SUBJECTIVE]: Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who is being evaluated today for a cough, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea.

S22 [SUBJECTIVE]: The patient's dandruff is also worsening.
S23 [ASSESSMENT AND PLAN]: I advised continuation of fluids, rest.
